title: Recognise and factorise a difference of two squares

source_reference.notes: Original Edexcel 4MA1 Higher-style item for the Year 10 quadratics MVP. Edexcel pivot metadata applied.

student_prompt: Show your working and give your answer in factorised form.

error_category_mapping.diagnostic_sentence: This is a difference of two squares: x^2 - 9 = x^2 - 3^2. It needs opposite signs in the brackets.
The middle terms must cancel. Opposite signs make +3x and -3x cancel to leave x^2 - 9.

hint_ladder.title: What special pattern might this be?
hint_ladder.prompt: Look for a squared term minus another squared value. This structure has a special factorisation pattern.

hint_ladder.title: Pick a starting move
hint_ladder.prompt: Rewrite the constant as a square first, then think about two brackets whose middle terms cancel.

hint_ladder.title: A common slip
hint_ladder.prompt: Many students use matching signs and accidentally create a middle term. This pattern needs opposite signs so the middle terms disappear.

hint_ladder.title: The general pattern
hint_ladder.prompt: For any a^2 - b^2, use the structure (a - b)(a + b). Apply this pattern to your expression; do not copy an example.

common_errors: tries to find two numbers that add to 0 without seeing the pattern
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is recognising the expression as a difference of two squares.

common_errors: uses the same sign in both brackets
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is using opposite signs so the middle terms cancel.

mark_scheme_notes: Award 1 mark for recognising 9 as 3^2 or using the difference-of-squares structure; 1 mark for correct brackets.
examiner_report_notes: Common errors expected: treating x^2 - 9 as not factorisable, or using same-sign brackets.
metacognition_prompt: Before you start, what special pattern might this expression match?
